title: Finite-support assembly of degreewise tensor-Hom comparisons
statement: Let A,B be commutative rings, φ:A→B a ring map, F:RingSiteModules(A)→RingSiteModules(B) an additive functor with objects equal to the specified scalar extensions [def-pc-perfect-rhom-base-change-map], and P,Q cochain complexes of A-module sheaves. Fix n∈ℤ and assume P^p is zero for p outside some integer interval [a,b]. Suppose for each p there exists an isomorphism g_p:F(Hom_A(P^p,Q^(p+n)))→Hom_B(F(P^p),F(Q^(p+n))) satisfying the normalized equation g_p(b⊗f)(c⊗x)=bc⊗f(x) on the identity slice object over every site object. Let t:F(Hom_A^bullet(P,Q)^n)→Hom_B^bullet(F(P),F(Q))^n be any module-sheaf map. Suppose every product coordinate of t satisfies (t(b⊗f))_p(c⊗x)=bc⊗f_p(x), using the shared product projections of [def-pur-hom-complex] and the pure tensors and evaluations of [def-pc-perfect-rhom-base-change-map]. Then t is an isomorphism. There is no projectivity hypothesis on P and no chain-map hypothesis on t; those belong to separate steps.

proof.text: The projections of homComplex_exists give a limiting product fan. Outside [a,b], P^p=0, so both Hom_A(P^p,Q^(p+n)) and Hom_B(F(P^p),F(Q^(p+n))) are zero; scalar extension preserves zero modules. Products of these families thus identify with their products over the finite integer interval. The empty interval is permitted.

Use ordinary scalar extension at the unique object and lem-weil-pbc-tensor-finite-product, with the commutativity isomorphism if needed, to commute scalar extension with this finite product. Follow by the finite product of the supplied g_p isomorphisms to obtain an isomorphism k with t's source and target.

The supplied formula for each g_p shows that each projection of k sends b tensor f, evaluated on c tensor x, to bc tensor f_p(x). The hypothesis on t gives the identical formula. Pure tensors generate both scalar extensions, and evaluation at the identity slice object detects internal-Hom sections on this one-object site. Hence all product projections of t and k agree; the product universal property gives t=k, so t is invertible.

theorem boundedRingHom_extension_degree_isIso
    {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] (φ : A →+* B)
    (F : RingSiteModules A ⥤ RingSiteModules B)
    (hF : ∀ M, F.obj M = SheafOfModules.changeOfRings (ringSiteMap φ) M)
    (hadd : F.Additive) (P Q : CochainComplex (RingSiteModules A) ℤ) (n : ℤ)
    (hb : ∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ p : ℤ, p < a ∨ b < p → IsZero (P.X p))
    (hterms : ∀ p : ℤ,
      ∃ g : F.obj (SheafOfModules.homObj (R := CochainComplex.onePointRingSheaf A)
          (P.X p) (Q.X (p + n))) ⟶
        SheafOfModules.homObj (R := CochainComplex.onePointRingSheaf B)
          (F.obj (P.X p)) (F.obj (Q.X (p + n))),
        IsIso g ∧ ∀ (U : (Discrete PUnit.{u + 1})ᵒᵖ) (b c : B)
          (f : (SheafOfModules.homObj (R := CochainComplex.onePointRingSheaf A)
            (P.X p) (Q.X (p + n))).val.obj U) (x : (P.X p).val.obj U),
          ((g.val.app U (ringExtensionPure φ F hF _ U b f)).app
            (op (Over.mk (𝟙 U.unop)))) (ringExtensionPure φ F hF (P.X p) U c x) =
          ringExtensionPure φ F hF (Q.X (p + n)) U (b * c)
            ((f.app (op (Over.mk (𝟙 U.unop)))) x))
    (t : F.obj ((homComplex (R := CochainComplex.onePointRingSheaf A) P Q).X n) ⟶
      (homComplex (R := CochainComplex.onePointRingSheaf B)
        ((ringExtensionComplex F hadd).obj P) ((ringExtensionComplex F hadd).obj Q)).X n)
    (ht : ∀ (p : ℤ) (U : (Discrete PUnit.{u + 1})ᵒᵖ) (b c : B)
      (f : (homComplex (R := CochainComplex.onePointRingSheaf A) P Q).X n |>.val.obj U)
      (x : (P.X p).val.obj U),
      ringHomEvaluate ((ringExtensionComplex F hadd).obj P)
        ((ringExtensionComplex F hadd).obj Q) n p U
        (t.val.app U (ringExtensionPure φ F hF _ U b f))
        (ringExtensionPure φ F hF (P.X p) U c x) =
      ringExtensionPure φ F hF (Q.X (p + n)) U (b * c)
        (ringHomEvaluate P Q n p U f x)) : IsIso t
